notes: Units are RAW token amounts per one whole (1e18) share, never percentages.
The decimals field is documentation and is checked against the chain at deploy time; a mismatch stops the run.
WEIGHTS. 40% NVDA, 30% PONS, 30% CASHCAT, sized against marks/4663.json on the date below. One share came to $99.84: NVDA 40.0%, PONS 30.0%, CASHCAT 30.0%.

Those weights are true on the day they were set and never again. A Stack holds FIXED QUANTITIES, not percentages — nothing rebalances, so the moment any of the three moves the weights move with it. That is the design, not a defect: you are wrapping a position, and a position drifts. The percentages describe the recipe's starting point and nothing else.

And two of the three prices are marks, not feeds. Neither PONS nor CASHCAT has an oracle on this chain, so their legs were sized against a number a person typed. A better number changes what 30% should have been; it does not change what was created, because unitsPerShare is immutable once a basket exists.

THIS SUPERSEDES THE FIRST ROBOT, at stack id 1, share token 0x334a76Bd1F4dF02a74b00315A94F6D740E372955. That one was written before anyone had a price for PONS or CASHCAT and was sized on fraction-of-supply instead. With real marks it came to $7,599 a share with NVIDIA at 0.03% of it — a PONS bag wearing a chipmaker as a garnish. It never minted a single share, so nothing was lost, but it cannot be edited: a recipe is fixed at creation. The only fix is a second basket and a freeze on the first.

The `supersedes` key below is what lets the deploy script open a second basket under a symbol it already carries. Without it the run refuses, which is the correct default — silently opening two ERC-20s with one symbol is how nobody can tell which is real.
